name: garmintools
desc: Interface to the Garmin Forerunner GPS units
why: Talks to Garmin GPS units over their binary serial protocol, a rare look at undocumented device communication.

brief.what_it_is: garmintools is a set of command-line tools for Garmin Forerunner GPS units, according to the one-line description in the package metadata. The package lists six executables: garmin_dump, garmin_gchart, garmin_get_info, garmin_gmap, garmin_gpx, and garmin_save_runs. From their names, the tools appear to read device data and export or chart it, but I could not confirm their inputs and outputs from the project pages. The scout notes say it talks to the units over their binary serial protocol.
brief.why_it_exists: The scout notes describe it as a rare look at undocumented device communication with Garmin GPS units. I could not find the author's own framing because the project page did not load its content.
brief.standout: Per the scout notes, it reverse-engineers or speaks Garmin's binary serial protocol directly, which is unusual for a GPS device. I could not verify this from the project's own pages.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage is on the Google Code Archive, a read-only store for projects hosted on Google Code, which shut down in 2015, so the project is archived there. I found no release date, commit date, or maintenance note because the pages returned only a JavaScript-required shell.
brief.caveats: The homepage and wiki both returned empty shells that require JavaScript, so I read no README, documentation, or command examples. The description and protocol claims come from package metadata and scout notes, not from the project itself. No license, platform, or hardware-model list was visible. The brew caveats field is empty.
